sources: Saunders/Inman/Eberhart via Atlas of Limb Prosthetics (oandplibrary.org/alp/chap13-01): potential 7-cm compass-gait displacement reduced to 5 cm by pelvic motions
Chambers & Sutherland 2002 J Am Acad Orthop Surg (Practical Guide to Gait Analysis): COM vertical rise/fall about 4 cm
Della Croce et al. review via J Biomech 2014 S0021929014000888: whole-body COM peak-to-peak ~5 cm vertical at natural speed
pelvisVerticalM.note: Pelvis vertical tracks COM vertical within millimetres. Excursion shrinks with shorter steps (Gard & Childress 2001), so the 0.707-scaled plan should read at the low end.

sources: Chambers & Sutherland 2002 JAAOS: COM total side-to-side displacement about 5 cm
Della Croce et al. review via J Biomech 2014 S0021929014000888: whole-body COM peak-to-peak ~5 cm mediolateral at natural speed
pelvisLateralM.note: Pelvis lateral tracks COM lateral. Same short-step caveat as vertical.

sources: Bonnefoy & Armand 2015 (unige:81179 Normal Gait): pelvis frontal-plane ROM around 8 deg
Perry & Burnfield via Northwestern VACMARL Module 4 slides: contralateral drop ~4 deg + ipsilateral drop ~4 deg over stance
pelvicObliquityDeg.note: Range over the stride (max-min), not single-side drop.

sources: Bonnefoy & Armand 2015 (unige:81179): transverse-plane pelvis ROM 8-10 deg depending on walking speed
Perry & Burnfield via VACMARL Module 4: pelvis rotates ~10 deg transverse (5 deg forward each side)
Murray et al. 1967 Phys Ther (Patterns of Sagittal Rotation of the Upper Limbs in Walking): free-speed (1.54 m/s) total shoulder excursion 32 +- 10 deg, fast 39 +- 12 deg
Vorontcova et al. 2022: shoulder flexion-extension ROM 24.6 +- 3.4 deg in healthy young males
Romkes & Bracht-Schweizer 2017 Gait & Posture: shoulder flexion amplitude drops with walking speed (speed-matched reading required)
Collins et al. 2009 Proc R Soc B (Dynamic arm swinging): slow speeds yield very-low-amplitude arm swing (after Craik et al. 1976)
shoulderFlexExtDeg.note: Free-speed band; at slow SC-05 speeds expect the low end or below. Over-amplitude (above band) is the Fable flag under test, not small swing.

sources: Murray et al. 1967 Phys Ther: free-speed total elbow excursion 30 +- 11 deg, fast 40 +- 13 deg (lower edge of the free-speed spread)
Romkes & Bracht-Schweizer 2017 Gait & Posture: elbow flexion amplitude drops with walking speed
elbowFlexExtDeg.note: Free-speed excursion 30+-11 deg; band low edge covers slow-speed shrinkage. Only excursion (range) is banded, not the mean angle.

sources: Bonnefoy & Armand 2015 (unige:81179 Trunk Segment): trunk sagittal inclination around 0 deg with ROM around 3 deg
trunkLeanMeanDeg.note: Source gives the mean (~0 deg); the +-5 deg envelope edges are UNSOURCED generosity, not literature. Trunk ROM itself (~3 deg) is reported alongside, unbanded.

sources: Murray et al. 1967 Phys Ther: upper-limb motion coincides with the contralateral lower limb, opposite the ipsilateral (simultaneous opposition)
Yegian 2012 thesis (Roles of muscles in arm swing): arm extended at ipsilateral heel-strike, flexed halfway through the stride
armLegPhaseLag.note: Lag of max shoulder-vs-ipsilateral-thigh anti-correlation, in cycle fractions; 0 = simultaneous opposition (the Murray anti-phase). +-0.15 tolerance edges UNSOURCED.
